cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. That is below the 40 to 60% typically seen in production systems of this complexity, and it means a regression can reach production unchallenged.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, eight months ago, took over three hours to complete, and deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. That concentration of capability and absence of recovery process means a failed deployment remains broken for hours while recovery depends on one person being reachable. The risk compounds during on-call handoffs and scheduled leave.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: Production database credentials rest with a single engineer on a month-to-month contract, with no documented handover process if that person leaves. This creates a critical dependency: there is no way to regain access to production data if the engineer becomes unavailable, and no procedure to transfer credentials to a replacement. The company has no compensating control. Immediate action is required to document credential management, distribute access across at least two people, and establish a tested handover procedure.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy. The company has no defined process for handling data-subject deletion requests under applicable privacy regulations. This combination creates regulatory exposure: a subject can request erasure and the company has no procedure to fulfill it, and data persists in production indefinitely after it is no longer needed for its original purpose.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no gate in continuous integration to block deployments below a defined threshold. The last three production incidents originated in untested edge cases, each requiring manual intervention to resolve. Deployments are performed manually with no documented rollback procedure, meaning a defect that reaches production stays live until someone capable of direct intervention is available. The combination leaves the system vulnerable to preventable failures during its growth phase.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table, with no hashing or salting applied. This means any database compromise exposes every user credential to an attacker without computational cost. Customer data confidentiality depends entirely on database access controls, leaving no compensating control. The company should implement bcrypt or a comparable key derivation function before the next production deployment.

The most recent deployment took four hours and required manual SSH access by a single engineer, with no documented or tested rollback procedure. Manual deployments at this stage create a sustained window where a bad release stays live while recovery depends on one person being reachable. We recommend automation for deployment and rollback, with at least one dry-run exercise of the rollback path before the next production change.

Code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention. While this does not expose data or availability, inconsistent conventions slow onboarding and make it harder for reviewers to distinguish intentional from accidental variation. Adding a comment-style rule to the linter is low-cost; we recommend it as a foundation for clearer code review signals.
